account:
Today’s clearest unusual business is the builder’s installation of eight lanterns in the great hall. The builder invited me to inspect the lighting tomorrow at eighteen hundred, saying no accounts or approvals were needed, just my opinion. I approved the time, and the secretary recorded it in the updated appointment book. This may simply be an improvement to the hall; I have no confirmed evidence of an event behind it.

At afternoon tea, my neighbour mentioned chatter about bakery decorations but had seen none personally. The neighbour later identified Townsfolk 02 as the source, whose talk of bakery lights and a bridge or port change was confused. The neighbour said the baker knew of no celebration. The secretary likewise has no confirmed information about bakery decorations. I cannot yet connect these rumours to the hall lighting or conclude that a celebration is planned.

Town accounts were not available for my office review. The secretary has not received the figures or further correspondence, and I do not know who holds the figures. I asked the secretary to check existing council records to identify the responsible person and request them, and to set aside council letters for tomorrow. I missed the secretary’s final words while leaving.

I also saw freight near the town hall carrying a sack of bread and holding an emerald this evening. I do not know its destination or purpose; this alone does not establish anything unusual. I am now home at nineteen hundred as scheduled. Tomorrow includes the mill grain inspection, regular office business and tea, followed by the confirmed great hall lighting inspection.
